summary: 9 new test files created for audit, deregister, hooks, install, join, peers, policies, sockutil, and uninstall CLI commands. All files compile and tests pass. However, the 'success path' tests for audit/peers/policies/hooks bypass command logic entirely by calling socketGet/socketPost directly instead of invoking RunE, leaving actual command output formatting untested. hooks_test.go lacks required table-driven tests. Helper function duplication exists between sockutil_test.go and status_test.go.

tests_checklist.item: All 9 test files exist and compile
Test helpers use t.Helper(), t.TempDir(), t.Cleanup()
deregister_test.go and join_test.go clean up package-level variables with t.Cleanup
Table-driven tests in hooks_test.go for list/verify scenarios
Success-path tests actually invoke command RunE logic
Tests verify command output strings, not just HTTP status codes

code_quality_checklist.item: Follows existing test patterns from status_test.go, state_test.go
No code duplication between test helpers
No dead code or commented-out code

security_checklist.item: No hardcoded secrets in test files
No sensitive data in test assertions

architecture_checklist.item: Test files co-located with source in cmd/plexd/cmd/
All tests in package cmd (not cmd_test)

architecture_findings.description: startTestSocketServer() in sockutil_test.go duplicates startFakeAgent() from status_test.go. Both create Unix socket HTTP servers with identical lifecycle management (t.TempDir, t.Cleanup, polling readiness loop). startTestSocketServer accepts a generic http.Handler while startFakeAgent takes a StateSummary — the former is more general but creates unnecessary duplication.
architecture_findings.fix: Remove startTestSocketServer. Use startFakeAgent where StateSummary is needed, or refactor startFakeAgent to optionally accept an http.Handler parameter.

issues_found.description: TestAuditCommand_SuccessPath does not test runAudit(). It creates a fake agent then calls socketGet() directly, verifying HTTP 200. This tests sockutil.go, not audit.go. The actual audit command output ('audit collection status not yet available') is never verified.
issues_found.fix: Either inject the socket path into runAudit (requires refactoring audit.go to accept a socket path) or test the full command via rootCmd.Execute() with a socket path override. At minimum, verify the output string.

issues_found.description: TestPeersCommand_SuccessPath is identical to TestAuditCommand_SuccessPath — calls socketGet('/v1/state') directly, never invokes runPeers(). Does not verify 'peer listing not yet available' output.
issues_found.fix: Same as TE1-1. The test should verify command-specific output, not just that an HTTP server responds with 200.

issues_found.description: TestPoliciesCommand_SuccessPath is identical to audit and peers — calls socketGet('/v1/state') directly, never invokes runPolicies(). Does not verify 'policy listing not yet available' output.

All hooks tests (list empty, list with hooks, verify, reload) call socketGet/socketPost directly instead of invoking runHooksList/runHooksVerify/runHooksReload. The actual command logic is untested: tabwriter formatting (hooks.go:75-84), checksum truncation >12 chars (hooks.go:79-81), verify WARN/OK output (hooks.go:118-123), reload Status/Hooks count output (hooks.go:160-161).
issues_found.fix: Tests should invoke the RunE functions or the command via rootCmd.Execute(). Verify actual formatted output: tabwriter columns, truncated checksums, WARN/OK lines, status/hooks count.

issues_found.description: TestHooksListCommand_RunE claims to test RunE but actually just decodes a JSON response from a mock server. Assertion checks len(got)==1 and got[0].Name=='hook-a' — this tests json.Decode, not the command's tabwriter output.
issues_found.fix: Replace with a test that calls runHooksList and captures the tabwriter-formatted output buffer.

issues_found.description: Review criteria requires 'Table-driven tests used in hooks_test.go for list/verify scenarios with multiple hook configurations'. hooks_test.go contains zero table-driven tests — each scenario is a separate function.
issues_found.fix: Refactor hooks list and verify tests to use table-driven pattern: []struct{name string, hooks []api.HookInfo, wantOutput string} with t.Run subtests.

issues_found.description: startTestSocketServer duplicates startFakeAgent from status_test.go. Both functions: create tmpDir via t.TempDir(), listen on Unix socket, start http.Server in goroutine, register t.Cleanup for shutdown+remove, poll for socket readiness.
issues_found.fix: Remove startTestSocketServer. Either reuse startFakeAgent where applicable, or extract a shared helper to a test_helpers_test.go file that both can use.

issues_found.file: cmd/plexd/cmd/peers_test.go:11, deregister_test.go:9, hooks_test.go:152, install_test.go:9, join_test.go:9, uninstall_test.go:9
issues_found.description: Help tests use cmd.Help() directly (e.g., peersCmd.Help()), while existing tests (logs_test.go:9, status_test.go:60, root_test.go:9) use rootCmd.SetArgs(['cmd', '--help']) then rootCmd.Execute(). Inconsistent pattern.
issues_found.fix: Use the existing pattern: rootCmd.SetArgs(['peers', '--help']); rootCmd.Execute() for consistency.

issues_found.description: ConfigError tests set rootCmd.SetOut/SetErr but don't reset to nil after rootCmd.Execute() returns error. Other tests in the same files (Help tests) DO reset. The existing pattern in status_test.go:18-31 also doesn't reset, so this is consistent with pre-existing code, but inconsistent within the same file.
issues_found.fix: Add defer to reset: defer func() { rootCmd.SetOut(nil); rootCmd.SetErr(nil) }() after SetOut/SetErr calls.

issues_found.description: Tests that call rootCmd.Execute() with '--config /nonexistent/path' modify the package-level cfgFile variable via cobra flag parsing. No t.Cleanup restores the default value. While existing tests have the same issue, the review criteria explicitly required cleanup for these tests.
issues_found.fix: Add t.Cleanup to save and restore cfgFile: old := cfgFile; t.Cleanup(func() { cfgFile = old })

suggested_improvements: Extract a shared test helper (e.g., in helpers_test.go) that can create either a generic HTTP Unix socket server or a StateSummary-based fake agent, replacing both startFakeAgent and startTestSocketServer

For commands that use defaultSocketPath() (audit, peers, policies, hooks), consider adding a package-level var socketPathOverride that tests can set via t.Cleanup to enable full command execution testing

Add output-assertion tests that verify the actual printed strings: 'audit collection status not yet available', 'peer listing not yet available', 'policy listing not yet available', tabwriter-formatted hooks output
Add a TestHooksList_ChecksumTruncation test verifying checksums >12 chars are truncated with '...' (hooks.go:79-81)
next_steps: Fix TE1-1 through TE1-4: Rewrite success-path tests for audit, peers, policies, and hooks to actually invoke command RunE functions and verify output
Fix C2-1: Add table-driven tests to hooks_test.go for list/verify with multiple hook configurations
Fix Q3-1: Consolidate startTestSocketServer and startFakeAgent into a shared helper
Fix TE4-1: Add t.Cleanup for package-level variable restoration in deregister_test.go and join_test.go
